X10.THD_EXCLUSIVE_DOC: Normal operation: Triggerhappy (Volumio's key service) reads all files in /etc/triggerhappy/triggers.d – Volumio's audio.conf and this plugin's file. When switched on: 1) After the plugin starts it checks that Triggerhappy is running; after the delay Triggerhappy is restarted (keys do not respond for 1–2 seconds). 2) From then on Triggerhappy reads only /run/x10remote/triggers.d/x10remote.conf. 3) This file contains the assignments of your profiles and a copy of all commands from audio.conf and other Triggerhappy files unless a profile assigns the key differently – so keyboards and other remotes keep working and nothing runs twice. Changes to audio.conf are picked up automatically. 4) audio.conf itself is not modified, moved or renamed. Back to normal: when this option or expert mode is switched off, when the plugin is disabled or uninstalled, and after every reboot (until it switches again after the delay). If switching fails, the plugin reverts automatically and reports it under "Show status". Only needed if Triggerhappy should use exclusively the plugin's assignments; not required for normal use.
X10.THD_EXCLUSIVE_DELAY_DOC: After the plugin starts it checks that Triggerhappy is running; after this time it is restarted in exclusive mode.

X10.SHELL_RISK_INTRO: With custom commands every key can run any shell command on this Volumio device. Concrete risks:
X10.SHELL_RISK_1: The web interface (port 7710) has no login: anyone who can open it on the network can store commands that run on the next key press.
X10.SHELL_RISK_2: Commands run with the rights of the Triggerhappy service (usually user "nobody"). They can change or delete world-writable files – e.g. music, playlists and profiles in "Internal Storage" – and read world-readable data.
X10.SHELL_RISK_3: A command can send data to the network or the internet and download and start programs.
X10.SHELL_RISK_4: Faulty commands (typos, endless loops, wrong deletions) can disturb playback, overload the device or delete files irrevocably.
X10.SHELL_RISK_5: Commands copied unchecked from the internet can be intentionally harmful.
X10.SHELL_RISK_LAN: As long as the Volumio device is not reachable from the internet (no port forwarding in the router, no "exposed host"/DMZ, guest Wi-Fi separated), this is not particularly dangerous: an attacker would already have to be inside your home network – and could operate Volumio anyway.
X10.SHELL_RISK_ADVICE: Recommendation: only switch this on if you need custom commands, only use commands you understand, and never expose the device directly to the internet.
X10.WEB_SHELL_LOCKED_EXPERT: Custom commands are locked. To enable: Volumio → Plugins → X10 RF Remote → Expert mode → "Allow custom shell commands".
